items.title: Neal Caine interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019
items.q: The interviewee discusses the general touring habits of bands like Count Basie's as described by the interviewer, but does not claim any personal interaction or professional relationship with Count Basie.

ctx.x: sets, nightly, and tour. You’ve got to work stuff out man. Especially when you get in a band, you get on the road, everything comes together. You know if you’re playing once a week or once every two weeks it’s hard to get continuity with your group. That’s a problem I’m having at least.

Yeah. I have a book, it’s called the Count Basie Bio-discography. These English jazz researchers man, they find this material. And you look at their itinerary. There’s hardly ever a day off, and so that sort of explains why the Great American Rhythm Section, man, they just played so much.
Yeah. Totally. And when you go on a tour with a band and you go out for three weeks or a couple of months, man, yeah, you can see the difference by the end of the tour. It’s really tight.
